market_summary: July PCE came in at 3.7% y/y headline (consensus 3.6%) with core 3.3% in line; Q2 GDP was unrevised at 1.5% and July durable goods rose 1.1% vs 0.4% expected. The US open is soft: S&P 500 7,671 (-0.1%), Nasdaq 100 -0.2%, SOX -0.4%, 10-year 4.66%, September hike odds ~40%; WTI $81.77, bitcoin $78,100, AUD/USD 0.717. Meta settled the 29-state teen-harm trial for up to $16.68B over 10 years and the stock is +0.6% after a $593 spike. Asia closed higher except the ASX 200 (-0.4% after the hot CPI): Nikkei +0.6%, Kospi +1.0%, Taiex +1.5%, Hang Seng +0.6%; Iran and Oman agreed a 7-mile temporary Hormuz corridor but Iran says the strait stays shut pending US sanctions relief, and Canada matched the new US 50% tariffs from September 8. Ahead in AEST: Nvidia ~6:30am Thursday (consensus $92.2B revenue, Q3 bar $104.2B, options imply 5.4%) with Salesforce the same session, Marvell ~6:30am Friday, and Warsh at Jackson Hole 12am Saturday.

AMZN.reason: Trading at $259.24 intraday, down 0.7% at 10:36 ET after the July PCE print (core 3.3% y/y, in line). New today: AWS agreed to buy DuckLabs, the Amsterdam maker of DuckDB, undisclosed price, closing as soon as next month with DuckDB staying MIT-licensed under its foundation; Charter is bundling discounted Prime Access for Spectrum Internet Assist customers; and Reuters says Moonshot AI is negotiating revenue-share hosting deals for Kimi K3 with Amazon, Microsoft and Google. All incremental to AWS; with $220B capex and the state antitrust suits capping the multiple, hold.

AXOS.reason: Trading at $98.66 intraday, down 0.2% at 10:22 ET, and no company news since Tuesday's NYSE Texas dual listing; only 13F position chatter. Benchmark's $120 target and 17% ROE still support holding.

BABA.reason: Hong Kong 9988 closed Wednesday at HK$116.60, up 2.1%, 3.5% above the HK$112.70 placing price, and the ADR is $121.01, up 1.3% intraday at 10:36 ET. The placement completed today: 710M new shares for ~HK$80B, ~60% (HK$47.9B) earmarked for global computing infrastructure and ~40% (HK$31.9B) for AI data centres and cloud. Alibaba also released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (6B active parameters, a preview of Qwen 4), and a plaintiff firm filed a routine securities class action tied to the placement drop. Two sessions above the placing price is progress but not a base; keep watching for a hold above HK$117-118 before adding.

ENPH.reason: Trading at $37.12 intraday, down 0.6% at 10:37 ET. No new tariff or policy action today: the Section 232 polysilicon minimum import price from Aug 7 remains the operative policy and the only fresh item is commentary on possible government equity deals for US solar makers. Q3 revenue guide of $290-320M is still below last year, so stay on the sidelines until residential demand stabilises.

FIGR.reason: Trading at $37.94 intraday, down 7.8% at 10:33 ET with a $37.17-40.50 range, giving back Tuesday's 6.5% gain. No press release, SEC filing, analyst note or peer move explains it (UPST flat, SOFI -0.4%, bitcoin -1.4%), so it reads as profit-taking in a thin, volatile name. Q2 revenue +121% to $198.8M and Bernstein's $70 target are unchanged; hold, but check for a filing if the drop extends.

GOOGL.reason: Trading at $342.28 intraday, down 1.35% at 10:37 ET, now ~4% under the 50-day near $358. Nothing new on fundamentals: Moonshot AI is in talks to have Google Cloud host its Kimi K3 model on revenue share, Verizon coverage of Gemini handling most inbound calls follows Monday's partnership, and Courthouse News reports the search-remedies judge told the DOJ and Google to settle details of the oversight body (article not retrievable). Cloud +82% and the ~$200B TPU cloud case are intact, so the dip remains an entry.

LDI.reason: Trading at $0.88 intraday, down 4.7% at 10:33 ET and still under the $1 NYSE threshold with the six-month cure window from the Aug 21 notice; no news today. Goldman is at Sell with a $1 target; compliance, reverse-split and dilution risk argue for reducing exposure.

META.reason: New today: Meta settled the 29-state teen-harm trial mid-trial for up to $16.68B (NYT says up to $17.1B), about 1.2% of market cap versus its own $1.4T worst case, and agreed to default daily time limits for teens, nighttime restrictions, stronger age assurance and expanded parental controls, with no admission. School-district and personal-injury cases and the New Mexico judgments ($375M and $567M) remain. The stock spiked to $593.34 then faded to $573.70, up 0.6% intraday at 10:36 ET, so much of the deal was priced after Tuesday's leak. The biggest overhang is gone, but with $125-145B capex and the shares still ~25% down YTD, hold until the capex return shows in numbers.

MRVL.reason: Flat at $240.00 intraday (-0.2%) ahead of Thursday's report (Fri ~6:30am AEST). Previews in the last 12h add nothing to the numbers: consensus $2.72B revenue and $0.93 EPS, Benchmark expects a Q3 guide of $3.03B and $1.09, and options now imply a 10.3% move versus the ~12% four-quarter average; consensus target is $291 (24 Buy, 5 Hold). Up ~160% YTD with the Google warrant deal priced in, so the guide is the whole trade; hold through it.

MU.reason: $934.80 intraday, up 0.2%, after Micron named Manish Bhatia President and COO and Scott DeBoer President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, with Sumit Sadana moving to senior advisor, effective immediately. Seoul closed constructive: SK hynix +0.6% to KRW 1,688,000 and Samsung +1.8% to KRW 261,500 with the Kospi +1.0%. The one new negative is TrendForce data showing YMTC at 14% of Q2 NAND bits and targeting the top spot by 2027, a NAND-price risk that matters more to SanDisk than to DRAM/HBM-weighted Micron. Nvidia tonight is the swing factor; hold.

NFLX.reason: $82.05 intraday, down 0.2%, and quiet since Wolfe's $95 target; the last 12h added only content items (Emily in Paris S6, a Top Boy prequel, Stella Artois tie-in) and a Motley Fool piece framing the test as sales growth (13.4% in Q2, 11.7% expected Q3), margin expansion and ads scale. Street target $96 with 25 Buys and 7 Holds; still ~36% under the 52-week high, so the valuation reset remains an add.

NVDA.reason: Trading $210.56 intraday, down 1.2%, about 70 minutes into the session with the print due after the close (Thu ~6:30am AEST); S&P 500 -0.1% and Nasdaq -0.2% at the open after headline PCE printed 3.7% y/y versus 3.6% consensus (core 3.3%, in line). New in the last 12h: options now imply a 5.4% move (~$280B), below the 6.5% priced in May and the 7.4% 12-quarter average, and the street wants networking near $17B (+~134% y/y) inside the $92.2B revenue consensus. Q3 bar ~$104B at ~75% gross margin, Rubin timing, the no-China assumption and the $500B customer-financing/$105B OpenAI guarantee questions are unchanged; hold and reassess after guidance.

RKT.reason: Down 2.3% to $13.97 intraday, the worst of the group, as the 10-year rose 2bp to 4.66% after headline July PCE came in at 3.7% y/y (3.6% consensus) and FedWatch put ~40% on a September hike. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year was 6.74% on Tuesday and MBS are weaker today, so refi volume gets no help; after the ~50% run the shares look fully priced, hold.

TSM.reason: ADR $416.76 intraday, down 0.2%, after Taipei closed 2330 at NT$2,415, up 0.6%, with the Taiex +1.5% to 45,833 on NT$804B turnover ahead of Nvidia. No new company news in the last 12h beyond a July bond-issuance filing and Apple's 2nm M6 on TSMC. With 40%+ 2026 growth guidance and up-to-10% 2027 price rises, the stock ~5% below the June NT$2,535 high remains a buy.

STRIPE.reason: Nothing new in the last 12h: an ASEAN local-payment-method rollout, a Branch gig-work survey and a Seeking Alpha piece on Stripe versus Adyen are all steady-state, not a mark event, so hold the private position. Marked at 2.27x cost: latest valuation ~$159B (2026-02) vs ~$70B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/stripes-valuation-soars-74-to-159-billion/).

OPENAI.reason: New in the last 12h: Bloomberg reports SoftBank is talking to banks about a $10-20B dollar/euro bond sale, possibly in September, to repay the $40B bridge loan behind its ~$65B OpenAI commitment due by October; that is SoftBank debt, not a new OpenAI round, so no mark change. Alongside the GSAM $6.6B GPU-backed package and the data-centre chief's exit, the funding stack is getting more levered ahead of a 2027 IPO; Nvidia's call may add colour on the $105B guarantee. Private, so hold. Marked at 5.43x cost: latest valuation ~$852B (2026-08) vs ~$157B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/openai-reportedly-completed-a-7-billion-employee-tender-offer/).
